name: Danube Delta
blurb: Reed seas, pelicans and sturgeon where the Danube meets the Black Sea.

tip.title: Thin out the carp
tip.text: Carp are a staple fish prey. Set Common carp to -100% and watch the pelicans, pike, otter and eagle that depend on them.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Danube Delta, Great white pelican, Dalmatian pelican). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Long summer light drives the growth of reeds, water plants and algae in the shallow lakes and channels.

nodes.name: Bacteria, fungi & invertebrates
nodes.desc: Break down dead reed, plant litter and carcasses and return nutrients to the water and mud.
Dominant grass of the delta marshes, forming vast reed beds. It grows in shallow water and tolerates brackish conditions. Birds such as pelicans nest in reedy vegetation.

nodes.name: Algae & phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the lakes and channels, nourished by river nutrients; the base of the open-water food chain.
A semi-aquatic rodent, one of the more recent arrivals to the delta. It feeds on water-lilies and other marsh plants.
Opportunistic canid recorded around the delta. GloBI records link it to muskrat, marsh frog, mute swan and wild boar.
Omnivore of the reed and forest edges, recorded eating frogs and other small animals among many foods.
A large water frog of the channels and marshes, and prey for many birds, snakes and mammals in the delta.
More than half of Eurasian breeding great white pelicans nest in the delta. They fish cooperatively in shallows, taking carp in Europe.
Takes fish, waterbirds and carrion, and sometimes steals food from other fish-eaters.

link_ideas.what: Beluga sturgeon migrate up the Danube to spawn, so the delta connects to river reaches far upstream.

story: The Danube Delta is Europe's second largest river delta and the best preserved on the continent, about 4,152 km². Reeds and floating reed islands fill its marshes. Over 320 bird species visit in summer, including great white pelicans and pygmy cormorants, and its waters hold carp, pike and beluga sturgeon.
matters: Plankton, worms, molluscs and fish in the shallow water feed the delta's birds. The delta, together with the Razim–Sinoe lagoons, is listed as a World Heritage Site.
